attribution.note: Marcus's own bullet point in his signed Substack post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: The normalisation says the same thing as the statement: a two-part, unhedged observation about the period up to March 2024.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair. Marcus named no population for 'most work', so the result depends on the contract's choice to count deployment efforts rather than companies. That choice is reasonable, but it decides the result.

evidence.note: A January 2024 review describes hallucination as a major obstacle to production deployment. This supports the 'hard' part only.

Secondary report of a small May–July 2023 survey: 13% of organisations had an LLM in production and 44% were only experimenting. It counts organisations, not efforts, and was fielded months before publication.
BCG survey of executives about AI and GenAI broadly. Its categories overlap and it does not isolate LLM projects, so it cannot settle the share.

reviews.rationale: e1 supports the claim that production deployment was hard. But nothing in the packet gives a representative, project-level measure showing that most LLM deployment work was still preliminary as of March 2024. The surveys count organisations or executives, are early or cover AI broadly, and point in that direction without settling it. Nothing contradicts the claim. Because the contract requires both parts, the claim is unresolved.
